name: objectcore
title: The factory that refuses to ship its own slop
brief: Show a senior technical audience what it means to put an AI-assisted build loop behind a gate that can actually fail — using the factory that generated this very demo, and letting it go red on stage.

audience.title: Platform architect
audience.cares: Whether the guarantees are mechanical or just conventions someone remembers to follow.

audience.title: Engineering leader
audience.cares: Whether this survives a team that did not build it, and what it costs to keep running.

evidence.ref: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json — derived, never hand-edited; check:catalog asserts it byte-matches a fresh derivation
dist/eval-evidence.json — the structured record every eval run writes, green or red
metrics/eval-history.jsonl — the recorded gate-health score per run, with its graded-case count
knowledge/entries/ — one file per captured lesson, reviewed in the PR that introduced it
packages/demo/src/gate.ts — the deterministic checks this very demo had to pass to be built

demonstrated live in the forge-a-plugin beat

beats.title: This slide deck had to pass a test
beats.narration: Before this deck could be built, something checked that every claim on it resolves to a source, that the demo you are about to watch has a fallback, and that the prose contains none of the marketing filler on its banned list. It failed the first two times.

claims.text: The build refuses to emit a deck whose gate is red.

props.headline: This slide deck had to pass a test
props.sub: and it failed the first two times

beats.title: Conventions rot; only checks hold
beats.narration: Every team here has a document describing how things are supposed to be done. The document is accurate on the day it is written. What actually holds a year later is the subset somebody turned into a check that fails the build.

beats.title: Derive the artifact, gate the derivation
beats.narration: So nothing here is maintained by hand. The plugin catalog is derived from the plugin directories by one pure function, and a check asserts the committed file byte-matches a fresh derivation. Hand-edit it and the build fails — not in review, in CI.

claims.text: The catalog is a derived artifact whose committed form is asserted to match a fresh derivation.

beats.title: Generating a plugin, live, against this repo
beats.narration: We are going to generate a real plugin now. Watch the left side: that is the plan it wrote before touching a file. Watch the bottom: that is the gate. I am going to stop it twice, and the second stop is where it gets something wrong.

claims.text: A generated plugin cannot enter the catalog until its skills are shown to fire and its agents to be delegated to.
Showing the agent's planning steps is a stated design principle for reliable agents, not a presentation choice.

live.task: Run /forge to generate a plugin: grill the request into a spec, plan its trigger surfaces and eval cases, scaffold it deterministically, then run the gate.
live.fallback: A recorded pass of this exact generation on a local branch, cued to the plan step. Cut on the word "meanwhile"; the eng leader calls it.
checkpoints: Approve the spec before the scaffolder writes a single file.
Read the generated trigger surfaces together before the gate runs.
Decide as a room whether the surface that misroutes gets reworded or the case gets cut.
live.expectedFailure: One generated skill description overlaps an existing one in the catalog, and the routing eval sends a prompt to the wrong skill. Let it go red on stage. Fix it by narrowing the description — never by weakening the case — and re-run.
traceSurfaces: the spec it grilled out, before any file is written
the eval gate output, including the red one

beats.title: What this costs you
beats.narration: It is slower to add a plugin here than to write one by hand. That is the trade: the gate rejects work that a human reviewer would have waved through, and somebody has to keep the checks honest as the platform underneath changes.

beats.title: The failures become the memory
beats.narration: When the gate goes red, a subagent diagnoses it and writes the lesson into a knowledge base the next run reads on the way in. The failure you just watched is already a file. The next generation starts knowing about it.

claims.text: Gate failures are captured as durable entries, reviewed in the pull request that introduces them.
Gate health is recorded per run, so a change that degrades it is visible rather than argued about.

beats.title: It went red on stage, and that is the argument
beats.narration: You watched the gate reject work that I wanted to ship. That is the only reason you should believe anything it passed.

props.quote: You watched the gate reject work that I wanted to ship.
props.attribution: the only reason to believe what it passed

beats.title: Take one check, not the factory
beats.narration: Do not copy this repository. Pick the one convention your team keeps re-litigating in review, and turn it into a check that fails the build. Then do the next one.

takeaway: The gate configuration, the eval-case format, and the reflection subagent that turns a red gate into a written lesson — all checked in at github.com/smithdak/objectcore, and runnable against a repository you already own.
